description: tests/build_first_valid_path.rs:122-128 — after asserting build_first_valid_path returned a valid chain, the test asserts that chain != bp_chain (the chain build_path picks first). This is non-obvious testing discipline: it guards against the failure mode where DFS ordering shifts such that build_path now picks a valid candidate first, making the iteration the test is trying to demonstrate vacuous. The panic message names exactly that scenario. A future contributor will suggest dropping this assertion ("if both helpers return a valid chain, the test passes — what more do you want?"). They are wrong: a passing test that doesn't exercise the code path it claims to is worse than a failing test. The assert_ne! turns "test silently became vacuous" into a hard failure. Worth defending verbatim in any PR review.
title: tc60 test's assert_ne! defensive guard is excellent
